question text: What is the function of the CTRL+C shortcut, and why is it useful when working on a computer?
a: It copies selected text or files to the clipboard without removing the original, allowing you to duplicate content quickly.
b: It deletes the selected text permanently from the storage drive.
c: It closes the currently active window to save system memory.
d: It pastes content that was previously stored on the clipboard.
e: It changes the selected font style to center-aligned text.
f: It opens the Command Prompt terminal window.

question text: What does the CTRL+V shortcut do, and why is it beneficial?
a: It cuts the selected text and stores it in a temporary folder.
b: It inserts (pastes) the most recently copied or cut item at the cursor position, saving time on retyping.
c: It selects all text and images in the current document.
d: It verifies spelling and grammar across the entire project.
e: It creates a new volume partition on the hard drive.
f: It saves the current document under a new file name.

question text: Why is the CTRL+Z shortcut considered one of the most important digital safety tools?
a: It permanently deletes all changes made during the past hour.
b: It zooms in to give a closer view of the current workspace.
c: It undoes the most recent action, allowing you to instantly recover from accidental deletions or mistakes.
d: It compresses all files into a ZIP archive to save disk space.
e: It locks the keyboard to prevent unauthorized access.
f: It restarts the operating system in Safe Mode.

question text: What is the purpose of the CTRL+Y shortcut, and how does it relate to CTRL+Z?
a: It yields control of the computer to a remote administrator.
b: It undoes two actions at a time instead of just one.
c: It creates a new y-aligned 3D grid in modeling software.
d: It redoes an action that was previously undone by CTRL+Z, or repeats the last command.
e: It opens the YouTube website in the default browser.
f: It selects all text from the cursor position to the end of the document.

question text: How does CTRL+X differ from CTRL+C, and when is it best to use it?
a: CTRL+X deletes the document, while CTRL+C only closes it.
b: CTRL+X copies only images, while CTRL+C copies only text.
c: CTRL+X removes the original item but does not save it to the clipboard.
d: CTRL+X exports the file directly to an external USB plash drive.
e: CTRL+X removes (cuts) the selected item from its original place and copies it to the clipboard, making it ideal for moving content.
f: CTRL+X and CTRL+C perform the exact same function with no difference.

question text: What does the CTRL+A shortcut do, and in which scenario is it most useful?
a: It aligns all paragraphs to the center of the page.
b: It automatically archives old files into a backup folder.
c: It activates the audio speakers on the computer.
d: It adds a new blank page or slide to the presentation.
e: It alphabetizes all the files inside the current directory.
f: It selects all items, text, or files in the current window at once, making it easy to copy, move, or delete everything quickly.

question text: Why should computer science students frequently use the shortcut CTRL+S while working?
a: It saves the current progress to the storage drive, preventing loss of work if the program crashes or the computer powers off.
b: It shuts down the computer safely at the end of the class.
c: It speed-checks the machine for viruses and security threats.
d: It opens the System Settings menu to adjust screen brightness.
e: It searches the internet for related reference images.
f: It shares the current project directly to social media.

question text: What does ALT+F4 do, and why should you use it with caution?
a: It refreshes the current webpage or folder view.
b: It immediately closes the currently active program or window, which can cause unsaved work to be lost if not saved first.
c: It formats the C: drive and reinstalls Windows.
d: It duplicates the active layer in a 3D modeling program.
e: It opens the fourth tab in your internet browser.
f: It turns off the computer monitor without closing applications.

question text: What is the purpose of holding ALT and pressing TAB (ALT+TAB), and why is it useful?
a: It inserts a five-space tab indentation in a coding editor.
b: It opens a new browser tab without closing the current one.
c: It displays an overview of all open applications and allows you to switch between them quickly without using the mouse.
d: It closes all open background tasks to speed up the SPU.
e: It tags the current file with an alternative file name.
f: It switches the keyboard language between English and Chinese.

question text: Consider the following file path: "E:\QA\Pictures\Screenshots\Screenshot1.png". Which statement accurately explains its structure?
a: "Screenshot1.png" is the root drive, and "E:\" is the file name.
b: "Paint" is the file extension, which means it is a program executable.
c: "QA" is a file extension, and "Screenshot1" is a subfolder inside "E:\".
d: "E:\" is the storage drive, "Screenshot1.png" is the file with a .png image extension, stored inside the "Screenshots" subfolder of "Pictures" under "QA".
e: The file path indicates an internet website URL rather than a local storage location.
f: "Pictures" is the main drive letter, and "E:\" is the name of the software used to open it.
